plain_explanation: A government-issued photo ID to verify who you are. Banks require either Aadhaar (biometric ID) or PAN card as primary KYC identity proof for all loan applicants.
where_to_obtain: Aadhaar: UIDAI website or nearest Aadhaar enrollment centre. PAN: Income Tax Department / NSDL / UTI portal (online or at authorised agent).
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 and publicly available bank requirements as of 2026. Verify with your bank before relying on this.

plain_explanation: A document confirming your current residential address. Accepted documents typically include Aadhaar, utility bills (not older than 3 months), passport, or voter ID.
where_to_obtain: Aadhaar from UIDAI. Utility bill from your electricity/water/gas provider. Voter ID from Election Commission.
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 as of 2026. Verify with your bank.

plain_explanation: Two to three recent colour passport-size photographs (white background). Required for the loan application form and for internal bank records.
where_to_obtain: Any photo studio. Some banks accept digital photographs uploaded to their portal.
source_note: Standard bank requirement as of 2026. Verify exact count with your bank.

plain_explanation: Payslips from your employer for the last 3 months, showing your gross and net salary, deductions, and employer details. Used to calculate your loan repayment capacity.
where_to_obtain: From your employer's HR department or payroll portal. Most corporate employers provide digital salary slips.
source_note: Standard bank requirement for salaried applicants as of 2026. Verify with your bank.

plain_explanation: A certificate from your employer showing your total salary and tax deducted at source (TDS) for the financial year. Used as income proof for the loan application.
where_to_obtain: From your employer's HR or accounts department. Must be issued by the employer; cannot be self-generated.
source_note: Standard bank requirement as of 2026. Some banks may accept ITR acknowledgement in lieu of Form 16.

plain_explanation: Bank account statements for the past 6 months showing your salary credits and financial behaviour. Banks use this to check income consistency and existing EMI obligations.
where_to_obtain: From your bank branch, netbanking portal, or bank's mobile app. Statements must be stamped/certified or downloaded from the bank's official portal.
source_note: Standard bank requirement as of 2026. Verify with your bank.

document_name: Property Title Deed / Agreement to Sell
plain_explanation: The legal document proving the seller's ownership of the property, or the draft agreement to sell between you and the seller. The bank needs this to assess the property's legal standing before disbursing the loan.
where_to_obtain: Obtained from the property seller. The title deed is registered at the Sub-Registrar Office. The agreement to sell is typically prepared by a lawyer.
source_note: Based on Registration Act 1908 and standard bank requirements as of 2026.

plain_explanation: A certificate issued by the Sub-Registrar confirming that the property is free from any registered mortgages, loans, or legal liabilities for a specified period. Essential for the bank's due diligence.
where_to_obtain: Sub-Registrar Office in the district where the property is located. Also available online through the Kerala Registration Department's e-Distrik portal.
depends_on: Property Title Deed / Agreement to Sell
source_note: Kerala-specific. Based on Kerala Registration Department guidelines as of 2026. Verify fee at your Sub-Registrar Office.

document_name: Adhesive Court Fee Stamp (Loan Agreement — Kerala)
plain_explanation: Court fee stamps affixed to the home loan agreement document as required under the Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act. The required denomination varies based on the loan amount.
where_to_obtain: Treasury offices, licensed stamp vendors, or Sub-Registrar offices across Kerala.
source_note: Kerala state-level requirement under Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act. Exact denomination depends on loan amount. Verify with your bank and registrar as of 2026.

plain_explanation: A certified extract from the Sub-Registrar's Index II register showing all registered transactions (sale, mortgage, lease) for a given property. Used by the bank to confirm ownership history and absence of existing encumbrances.
where_to_obtain: Sub-Registrar Office in the relevant district or via IGR Maharashtra (igrmaharashtra.gov.in) online portal.
depends_on: Property Title Deed / Agreement to Sell
source_note: Maharashtra-specific. Based on IGR Maharashtra guidelines as of 2026. Verify fee at your Sub-Registrar Office.

plain_explanation: In Maharashtra, loan agreements must be stamped using the franking machine at an authorised bank or e-Stamp from SHCIL. This is a state stamp duty on the loan agreement itself, separate from the property stamp duty. Approximately 0.1% of the loan amount, subject to a cap.
where_to_obtain: Authorised franking centres (most nationalised banks), or SHCIL e-Stamp portal (shcilestamp.com) or authorised e-Stamp vendors.
source_note: Maharashtra state-level requirement under the Maharashtra Stamp Act. Approx 0.1% of loan amount, capped. Verify exact amount with your bank and registrar as of 2026.

plain_explanation: Your Indian passport is the primary identity and citizenship document for NRI account opening. It proves you are an Indian national and must be valid (not expired) at the time of application.
where_to_obtain: Passport Seva Kendra in India, or Indian Embassy / High Commission / Consulate in your country of residence.
source_note: Based on RBI Master Direction on NRI accounts and FEMA 1999 as of 2026. Verify with your bank.

document_name: Proof of NRI Status (Valid Foreign Visa / Work Permit / Residence Permit)
plain_explanation: A document proving that you reside outside India for employment, business, or another purpose. A valid employment visa, work permit, or overseas residence permit is typically accepted.
where_to_obtain: Issued by the immigration or labour authority of the country where you reside. Must be current and valid.
source_note: Required under FEMA 1999 and RBI KYC Master Directions 2016. Verify acceptable document types with your bank as of 2026.

plain_explanation: A document confirming your current residential address abroad. Typically an overseas bank statement, utility bill, or official government-issued document showing your foreign address — not older than 3 months.
where_to_obtain: Foreign utility provider, overseas bank, or any official foreign authority. The document must be in English or accompanied by a notarised translation.
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 as of 2026. Verify acceptable documents with your bank.

plain_explanation: A document confirming a valid address in India (usually your family home or permanent address). Required even though you reside abroad, as the account is in India.
where_to_obtain: Aadhaar from UIDAI, or voter ID, or a recent Indian utility bill, or property ownership documents.
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 as of 2026. Some banks may waive this for fully overseas applicants.

plain_explanation: Permanent Account Number (PAN) card for income tax purposes. If you do not have a PAN, you must submit Form 60 (declaration that you do not have a PAN). Banks require this for transactions above specified limits.
where_to_obtain: PAN: Income Tax Department via NSDL (onlineservices.nsdl.com) or UTI portal. Form 60: Available at any bank branch or downloadable from the Income Tax Department website.
source_note: Required under the Income Tax Act 1961 and RBI KYC norms as of 2026.

plain_explanation: Two recent colour passport-size photographs with white background, taken within the last 6 months. Required for the account opening form.
where_to_obtain: Any photo studio. Many NRI applicants apply through online or courier-based NRI account opening processes where digital photographs are accepted.
source_note: Standard bank requirement as of 2026.

plain_explanation: A declaration confirming your NRI status and that the funds you are depositing comply with the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999. This protects both you and the bank in case of regulatory scrutiny.
where_to_obtain: Available from the bank where you are opening the NRI account. Must be filled, signed, and submitted along with the account opening form.
source_note: Mandatory under FEMA 1999 and RBI guidelines. As of 2026. Verify format with your bank.

document_name: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
plain_explanation: The primary legal document that transfers ownership of the property from seller to buyer. It must be executed (drafted and signed) before it can be presented for registration at the Sub-Registrar Office. Banks typically need this drafted before they release loan funds.
where_to_obtain: Prepared by a licensed document writer (deed writer) or a registered advocate. The final registered copy is issued by the Sub-Registrar Office.
source_note: Based on Registration Act 1908 and standard practice as of 2026. Lawyer fees vary widely; verify with a local advocate.

document_name: PAN Card of Buyer and Seller
plain_explanation: PAN cards of both the buyer and the seller are mandatory for property registration when the sale consideration exceeds Rs 5 lakh. The Sub-Registrar will not proceed without them.
where_to_obtain: Income Tax Department via NSDL or UTI portal.
source_note: Required under Section 139A of the Income Tax Act 1961 as of 2026.

document_name: Passport-Size Photographs of Buyer, Seller, and Witnesses
plain_explanation: Passport-size photos of the buyer, seller, and at least two witnesses. Required by the Sub-Registrar at the time of registration.
where_to_obtain: Any photo studio.
source_note: Standard Sub-Registrar requirement as of 2026. Verify exact count with your local Sub-Registrar Office.

plain_explanation: The official letter from the buyer's bank confirming that the home loan has been sanctioned. Required to demonstrate that the buyer has funds and for the bank to co-ordinate loan disbursement with the registration.
where_to_obtain: Issued by your bank after loan approval. Typically provided within 3-7 days of completing all loan formalities.
depends_on: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
source_note: Standard bank and registration requirement as of 2026.

plain_explanation: If there is an existing loan on the property (i.e., the seller still has a mortgage), the seller's bank must issue a No-Objection Certificate confirming they will release their charge on the property upon receiving the sale proceeds.
where_to_obtain: Issued by the seller's current lending bank. The seller must request this from their bank's loan department.
source_note: Required only if the property has an existing mortgage. Standard banking practice as of 2026.

plain_explanation: Issued by the Sub-Registrar, this certificate lists all registered transactions (sales, mortgages, leases) on a property over a requested period. Form 15 is issued if there are encumbrances; Form 16 is a nil-encumbrance certificate. Both buyer's bank and the Sub-Registrar will require this.
where_to_obtain: Sub-Registrar Office in the taluk where the property is situated. Also available via the Kerala Registration Department e-Distrik portal.
depends_on: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
source_note: Kerala-specific requirement under the Registration Act 1908 as of 2026. Verify fee at your Sub-Registrar Office.

plain_explanation: Stamp duty is a state tax on the sale deed. In Kerala, the rate is approximately 8% of the guideline value or market value (whichever is higher) for male buyers, and approximately 6% for female buyers. This must be paid before or at registration.
where_to_obtain: Paid at the Sub-Registrar Office or via the Kerala Registration Department portal. Payment is made in cash, DD, or online transfer as per current accepted modes.
depends_on: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
source_note: Kerala state subject. Approximately 8% (men) / 6% (women) of guideline value as of 2026. NOT regulated by RBI. Rates may change; verify with the Kerala Registration Department before your appointment.

plain_explanation: A separate fee payable to the Sub-Registrar for registering the sale deed. In Kerala, this is approximately 2% of the property guideline value.
where_to_obtain: Paid at the Sub-Registrar Office at the time of registration.
source_note: Kerala state subject. Approximately 2% of property guideline value as of 2026. NOT regulated by RBI. Verify with the Kerala Registration Department.

plain_explanation: Stamp duty is a state tax on the sale deed. In Maharashtra, the rate is approximately 6% for male buyers and 5% for female buyers (both as of 2026). Properties in Mumbai attract an additional 1% metro cess, bringing the effective rate to 7% (men) or 6% (women) in Mumbai.
where_to_obtain: Via SHCIL e-Stamp (shcilestamp.com), authorised franking centres, or the IGR Maharashtra portal (igrmaharashtra.gov.in). Must be obtained before presenting the deed at the Sub-Registrar Office.
depends_on: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
source_note: Maharashtra state subject under the Maharashtra Stamp Act. Approx 6% (men) / 5% (women) plus 1% metro cess in Mumbai as of 2026. NOT regulated by RBI. Verify current rates with IGR Maharashtra.

plain_explanation: A fee payable to the Sub-Registrar for registering the sale deed. In Maharashtra this is 1% of the property value, capped at Rs 30,000.
where_to_obtain: Paid at the Sub-Registrar Office at the time of registration.
source_note: Maharashtra state subject. 1% of property value, capped at Rs 30,000 as of 2026. NOT regulated by RBI. Verify with IGR Maharashtra.

plain_explanation: A certified extract from the Sub-Registrar's Index II register confirming the last registered owner and any existing mortgages or charges on the property. The buyer's bank typically requires this as part of their legal verification.
where_to_obtain: Sub-Registrar Office in the relevant district, or via the IGR Maharashtra portal (igrmaharashtra.gov.in).
depends_on: Sale Deed (Executed by Licensed Document Writer)
source_note: Maharashtra-specific. Based on IGR Maharashtra guidelines as of 2026.

document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
plain_explanation: Proof of the legal existence of your business. For a private limited company, this is the Certificate of Incorporation from MCA. For a partnership, it is the Partnership Deed. For a proprietorship, a trade license or Udyam Registration Certificate is accepted.
where_to_obtain: Private limited: MCA21 portal (mca.gov.in). Partnership deed: Prepared by a notary or advocate. Trade license: Local Municipal Corporation. Udyam: Udyam Registration Portal (udyamregistration.gov.in).
source_note: Based on publicly available bank requirements as of 2026. Type of document varies by entity structure.

plain_explanation: Government-issued certificate confirming your business is registered under GST. Banks require this for GST-linked current accounts. It confirms the business is operational and tax-compliant.
where_to_obtain: GST portal (gst.gov.in). Free. Apply online; certificate is issued within 3-7 working days of complete application submission.
depends_on: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
source_note: Required by most banks for GST-linked current accounts. Based on publicly available bank requirements as of 2026.

plain_explanation: Permanent Account Number (PAN) issued specifically to the company or firm (not the personal PAN of the owner). Required for all financial transactions and tax compliance.
where_to_obtain: Income Tax Department via NSDL (onlineservices.nsdl.com) or UTI portal. The business must apply with its Certificate of Incorporation or Partnership Deed.
depends_on: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
source_note: Required under Income Tax Act 1961 and RBI KYC norms as of 2026.

document_name: KYC of Directors / Partners / Proprietor (Aadhaar + PAN)
plain_explanation: Identity and address proof (Aadhaar and PAN) for each director, partner, or proprietor of the business. Banks must comply with Know Your Customer (KYC) rules for every person with significant control over the account.
where_to_obtain: Aadhaar: UIDAI. PAN: NSDL or UTI portal. All individuals must provide self-attested copies.
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 as of 2026.

plain_explanation: For private limited companies, a board resolution passed in a board meeting authorising the opening of the bank account and naming the authorised signatories. Partnerships and proprietorships submit an authorisation letter instead.
where_to_obtain: Prepared internally by the company secretary or a chartered accountant. Must be on company letterhead and signed by all directors.
depends_on: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
source_note: Standard bank requirement for companies. Based on publicly available bank requirements as of 2026.

plain_explanation: Document confirming the registered or operating address of the business. Accepted documents typically include a utility bill in the business name, lease or rental agreement, or property ownership document.
where_to_obtain: Utility bill from your electricity/water provider. Rental agreement from your landlord. Property document from the relevant authority.
source_note: Based on RBI KYC Master Directions 2016 as of 2026. Verify acceptable document types with your bank.

document_name: Latest 6 Months Bank Statement of Promoter
plain_explanation: Personal bank account statements of the proprietor, partners, or main director for the last 6 months. Banks use this to assess the promoter's financial standing and to detect any adverse credit behaviour.
where_to_obtain: From the promoter's personal bank, via netbanking or bank branch.
source_note: Standard bank requirement as of 2026. Some banks may waive this for well-established businesses.

document_name: Kerala Shops and Establishments Registration Certificate
plain_explanation: Mandatory registration for all commercial establishments (shops, offices, hotels, etc.) operating in Kerala. Banks accept this as valid proof of the business operating address in Kerala.
where_to_obtain: Kerala Labour Department / e-Suvidha portal (esuvidha.kerala.gov.in). Application submitted online; certificate usually issued within 7-15 working days.
depends_on: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
source_note: Requirement under Kerala Shops and Commercial Establishments Act 1960. Fee varies by number of employees. As of 2026, verify with Kerala Labour Department.

document_name: Maharashtra Shops and Establishments Registration Certificate (Gumasta)
plain_explanation: The 'Gumasta' licence is the registration certificate under the Maharashtra Shops and Establishments Act 2017. Required for all commercial establishments in Maharashtra. Banks in Maharashtra commonly require this as address proof for the business.
where_to_obtain: Maharashtra Labour Department portal (aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in) or Aaple Sarkar portal. Application submitted online.
depends_on: Certificate of Incorporation / Partnership Deed / Trade License
source_note: Requirement under Maharashtra Shops and Establishments Act 2017. Fee varies by establishment size. As of 2026, verify with Maharashtra Labour Department.
